title: Compare equivalent products before comparing price
premise: A shopper can misread a lower price as better value when the products are not on the same basis.
audience: Adults comparing a shortlist of similar products online.
customerMoment: The shopper has two options and is about to decide on price alone.
tension: Price looks decisive even when serving size or declared amount differs.
opportunity: Teach a short sequence: match the basis, then compare price.
decisionQuestion: Are these two offers actually the same thing?
desiredTakeaway: Price is useful only after the offers are matched.
whyItMatters: This prevents a false bargain without adding medical or legal claims.
supportingInsights: Two similar-looking offers can differ on serving basis or declared amount.
limitations: This packet does not compare specific brands.
